title: Threshold Cliffs x Strategic Capability Withholding: Modeling the Incentive to Park Just Below the Line

original_idea.body:
# Threshold Cliffs x Strategic Capability Withholding: Modeling the Incentive to Park Just Below the Line

**Problem:** Governance uses sharp thresholds with large obligation jumps; developers can tune disclosed capability to sit just below. Bunching incentive hollows the regime.

**Direction:** Build a game-theoretic/numerical model of bunching, then look for bunching evidence in public model-report distributions.

**Why it matters:** Predicts and partially tests a manipulation pattern, arguing for graduated obligations.

**Relevant context:** artificialintelligenceact.eu; arXiv:2402.08797.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (threshold gaming defeats governance) but catastrophic-risk link is indirect and partly theoretical.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Toy model + light empirical bunching check; guided, some economics background helps.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused two-part deliverable (model + data check) with few dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Modeling + public data, structural concern labs won't volunteer.

novelty.reasoning: Bunching at thresholds is a classic econ idea; applying it to compute/capability cliffs may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Threshold bunching is well-known in economics; the AI-capability application may be open.
